question_text:
State the output of this SQL query. Technician(TechnicianID, Name) contains (7, "Ari"),(8, "Bo"). Observation(DeviceID, TechnicianID, Kind) contains (10,7, "voltage"),(11,7, "temperature"),(12,8, "voltage"),(13,7, "voltage"). Treat output order as unspecified.

SELECT O.DeviceID FROM Observation O JOIN Technician T ON O.TechnicianID=T.TechnicianID WHERE O.Kind='voltage' AND T.Name='Ari';
adaptation_rationale: Add a two-table join to match the explicitly required between-two-tables SQL objective; retain filtered-query output reasoning. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: DeviceID values 10 and 13, in either order.
